description: SPACE VISION is a multidisciplinary Mexican team combining software engineering, artificial intelligence, and visual healthcare. Our mission is to explore astronaut visual health and Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) through scientific data analysis, intelligent monitoring, and interactive space mission simulations. We bring together expertise in technology, research, and visual rehabilitation to advance human health beyond Earth.
summary:
Long-duration spaceflight induces cephalic fluid shifts that can trigger Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), altering the optic nerve, retina, and ocular globe morphology. To address this challenge, we developed SPACEVISION Predictor for SANS, an experimental neuro-ophthalmological tracking platform that combines autonomous in-flight astronaut visual checks with ground clinical evaluations and -6° Head-Down Tilt Bed Rest (HDTBR) analog studies.

The system integrates five core ophthalmological parameters—spherical equivalent (hyperopic shift), axial length, OCT retinal thickness, intraocular pressure, and optic disc characteristics (Frisén grade and choroidal folds)—with microgravity exposure data. It provides independent per-eye (OD/OS) longitudinal tracking before, during, and after spaceflight (+30, +60, and +90 days), automated fundus image analysis in Python, an interactive 3D and SD-OCT ocular viewer, and exploratory pattern analysis across Stable, Worsens, and Unscanned scenarios without issuing automated fit-for-duty verdicts.

This is important because integrating functional and structural ocular biomarkers helps medical teams prioritize early clinical review and generate hypotheses on individual SANS susceptibility, subject to independent clinical validation.
details:
SPACEVISION Predictor for SANS (SANS Monitor) is an experimental neuro-ophthalmological surveillance platform designed to track ocular changes before, during, and after spaceflight (+30, +60, and +90 days). It integrates two complementary monitoring workflows:

1. Autonomous In-Flight Checks (Astronaut Check): Enables crew members to log visual symptoms, near-vision status, tonometer IOP readings, and retinal fundus captures for downlink to Ground Control.

2. Ground Clinical & -6° HDTBR Analog Evaluation (Scientific Module, 3D/OCT Viewer & Population Dashboard): Combines five core ophthalmological parameters—spherical equivalent (hyperopic shift), axial length, OCT retinal thickness (ΔTRT), intraocular pressure, and optic disc characteristics (Frisén grade and choroidal folds)—with experimental microgravity exposure (-6° Head-Down Tilt Bed Rest vs. 0° terrestrial controls).

Each eye (OD / OS) is evaluated independently into three operational triage states—Ready for review, Prioritize review, or Missing data—and compared against three canonical trajectories (Stable, Worsens, Unscanned). A Python Computer Vision pipeline analyzes fundus images (optic disc localization, Sobel rim sharpness, peripapillary edema halo, and choroidal fold detection), while an interactive 3D WebGL ocular globe and Cirrus SD-OCT workstation visualize posterior globe flattening, optic disc protrusion, and 9-sector ETDRS deviation maps.

Benefits & Intended Impact

- Early Triage Without Automation Overreach: Helps flight surgeons decide which eye and case to review first while explicitly displaying "Fitness not evaluated" until human clinical sign-off.

- Honest Missing-Data Tracking: Ensures an unscanned or delayed OCT measurement is flagged as Missing data rather than assumed stable.

- Research & Hypothesis Generation: Unifies functional and structural ocular biomarkers with NASA open-science context (OSDR, NTRS, DONKI, ISS telemetry) to explore individual SANS susceptibility patterns, generating testable hypotheses subject to independent clinical validation.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

- Web Backend & Frontend: PHP 8.3 (Laravel 11, Blade), HTML5/CSS3, JavaScript, Chart.js, and Three.js (WebGL 3D).

- Scientific & Computer Vision Microservice: Python 3.14 (FastAPI, Uvicorn), NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn, and Pillow.

- Database & DevOps: MySQL, GitHub Actions CI/CD, PHPUnit (82 automated tests), and Pytest (22 automated tests).

- AI Development Tools (Disclosed): Antigravity (IDE Extension), Codex, Gemini, and GPT 6.1 SOL, with all clinical rules and outputs verified by the team.

How It Is Creative

Rather than treating eye health as a single static score, SPACEVISION pairs a dual 3D WebGL + SD-OCT Digital Twin with real Python computer-vision fundus overlays (disc edge, edema halo, and choroidal fold ridge maps) and side-by-side orbital vs. -6° HDTBR cohort comparisons. It also includes an interactive guided walkthrough and an automated fallback architecture so clinical evaluation remains operational even offline.

Factors Our Team Considered

- Clinical Safety (Human-in-the-Loop): Strictly avoids automated fit-for-duty decisions.

- Per-Eye Independence: Tracks OD and OS separately so progression in one eye is never masked by stability or missing data in the other.

- Data Integrity: Refuses synthetic imputation for missing scans and preserves versioned NASA protocol traceability (e.g., NASA-STD-3001, NASA HRP SANS Evidence Report).

- Accessibility, Ethics & Multidisciplinary Governance: Designed with WCAG 2.2 AA high-contrast dark mode, zero-login judge access, and legal/bioethical oversight from our multidisciplinary team across clinical optometry, medicine, software engineering, international relations, and legal sciences.
